Write `/root/bench-runs/h4-671cf6e0/test/api-routes.test.mjs` (node:test + node:assert/strict, Node 22 built-ins only). Skill to load: tdd-workflow (if unavailable, follow these rules). Spec (source of truth): `/root/bench-runs/h4-671cf6e0/.team/notes/spec.md`, sections "Server" (concurrency, body draining) and "API". Use helpers in `/root/bench-runs/h4-671cf6e0/test/helpers.mjs` (read it: startServer, request (sends path byte-for-byte), postJson, booking, makeTempDir, removeDir, JSON_CT). Do NOT edit anything except your test file(s). Run: `cd /root/bench-runs/h4-671cf6e0 && node --test test/api-routes.test.mjs` (`node --test test/` is broken on Node 22). If a failure is a SERVER spec violation, keep the test and report the repro to me; never weaken it.

Project rules: no console.log; each file under 400 lines (split into `api-routes.test.mjs`, `api-list.test.mjs`, `api-concurrency.test.mjs` as needed); functions under 50 lines; temp dirs removed and servers stopped in after/finally; exact equality (assert.equal/deepEqual) for every value the spec names, including the full Content-Type string `application/json; charset=utf-8` (an extended or different value must fail). Start a fresh server (PORT=0, DATA_FILE in a temp dir) per describe block, or per test where state matters.

Tests:
1. GET /api/rooms → 200, json deep-equal `{"rooms":["Aurora","Borealis","Cosmos"]}`, content-type exact. Also `/api/rooms?x=1` → 200 same.
2. 404 `{"error":"not found"}` (exact deep-equal; content-type exact) for each of: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms`, `/api/Rooms`, `/api/rooms/`, `/api/bookings/` (GET and DELETE), `/api/bookings/1/` (GET and DELETE), `/api/bookings//1`, `/api/bookings/1/x` DELETE, `/nope`, `/index.html`, `/app.js/`, `//`, `/api`, `/api/` — and with methods GET, POST, PUT, DELETE for a few of them ("whatever the method"). Also `/api/bookings/?x` DELETE → 404 not found.
3. 405 `{"error":"method not allowed"}` exact: POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH/OPTIONS on `/api/rooms`; PUT/DELETE/PATCH/OPTIONS on `/api/bookings`; GET/POST/PUT on `/api/bookings/1`; `GET /api/bookings/abc` → 405; POST/DELETE on `/` and `/app.js`; OPTIONS `/`. HEAD on `/api/rooms`, `/api/bookings`, `/`, `/app.js` → status 405 (HEAD has no body; only check status). For non-HEAD 405s also check content-type exact.
4. DELETE route: create bookings id 1 and 2. DELETE `/api/bookings/01`, `/api/bookings/0`, `/api/bookings/-1`, `/api/bookings/1.0`, `/api/bookings/+1`, `/api/bookings/abc`, `/api/bookings/%31`, `/api/bookings/１` (full-width, send it percent-encoded as `/api/bookings/%EF%BC%91`), `/api/bookings/99` → each 404 `{"error":"booking not found"}` exact, and booking 1 still exists. DELETE `/api/bookings/1?x=2` → 204 (query stripped), raw body length 0, then GET shows booking 1 gone. DELETE again → 404 booking not found. 204 reply has no content-type requirement; assert raw body is empty.
5. GET /api/bookings list: create bookings in shuffled order then assert full deep-equal order: sort by date, then start, then room order Aurora<Borealis<Cosmos (NOT alphabetical-by-any-other-rule: include a case where room order matters at same date+start, e.g. Cosmos then Aurora then Borealis created at 2026-11-03 09:00-10:00 → listed Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos; include a date earlier lexicographically and later starts, e.g. 2026-11-02 23:00 before 2026-11-03 08:00; and start `09:00` with end `09:30` vs `09:00`-`10:00` different rooms). Each booking object must have exactly keys id, room, title, date, start, end (deepEqual on whole objects). POST 201 reply deep-equals `{id, ...fields}` with content-type exact; extra body keys (e.g. `"extra":1`, `"id":99`) are ignored → id is the server's, no extra key in reply or list.
6. `?date` filter: bookings on 2026-11-03 and 2026-11-04. `?date=2026-11-03` → only those (sorted). `?date=2026-11-03&date=2026-11-04` → first only. `?x=1&date=2026-11-04` → 2026-11-04 only. `?foo=bar` → all. `?date=2026-11-05` → `{"bookings":[]}`. `?date` (no `=`) → 400 `{"error":"date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date"}` exact. `?date=` → 400 same. `?date=bad`, `?date=2026-02-30`, `?date=2026-11-3`, `?date=%202026-11-03` → 400. Percent-decoding: `?date=2026%2D11%2D03` → 200 with the 2026-11-03 bookings. `?date=2026-11-03+` → 400 ('+' decodes to space). `?DATE=bad` → 200 all (param name case matters). `?dat%65=bad` → 400 (decoded name is `date`). Path with query only on `/api/bookings?date=bad` uses GET; POST `/api/bookings?date=bad` with valid booking still 201.
7. Content-Type exact on: 200 rooms, 200 bookings, 201, 400, 404, 405, 409, 413, 415 replies (one test that collects them).
8. Body draining: POST /api/bookings with Content-Type text/plain and a 5 MB body → reply 415 `{"error":"content type must be application/json"}` received (no ECONNRESET/EPIPE); POST with application/json and 5 MB body → 413 `{"error":"body too large"}`. Also a GET /api/rooms with a 1 MB body → 200. Use the helper's request() which writes the whole body.
9. Concurrency: fresh server; fire 20 POSTs of overlapping bookings (same room+date, different times all overlapping 09:00-10:00, e.g. start 09:00 end 10:00 with various titles) at once with Promise.all → exactly one 201, 19 × 409 whose error message is exactly `room is already booked from <s> to <e>` with the times of the created booking. Then 30 non-overlapping POSTs at once (different rooms/dates/times) → all 201, ids are unique and exactly the set 2..31; GET lists 31 bookings; restart server with the same DATA_FILE → still 31 bookings and next POST id 32. Also concurrent DELETEs of the same id (10 at once) → exactly one 204, nine 404 `booking not found`.

Report back: files written, test count, pass/fail summary, and any server spec violations with exact repro.

content.content: 1 # Meeting-room booking app — full spec (verbatim from the user; final, no questions allowed) 2 3 Constraints: Use only Node.js built-ins (no npm install). Node v22. Do not use the Fable model. 4 5 Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. 6 7 ## Server 8 - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. 9 - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 10 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 11 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 12 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 13 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. 14 - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. 15 - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. 16 - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. 17 - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. 18 19 ## API 20 - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. 21 - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. 22 - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. 23 - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. - `api-list.test.mjs` covers items 5 and 6: list ordering, extra POST keys, and the `?date` filter cases.
